newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa won't mediate in Angola - Mandela.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa won't mediate in Angola - Mandela.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela on Sunday pledged South Africa's support for Angola's peace process, but said Pretoria would not act as a mediator.

Deputy President Thabo Mbeki had flown to Luanda to brief President Jose Eduardo dos Santos on talks last week between a South African delegation and representatives of Angola's former rebel movement UNITA, Mandela said.
He told several thousand party faithful gathered to mark the 85th birthday of his ruling African National Congress that the talks with UNITA's leader Jonas Savimbi were "very fruitful".
"But we made it clear to him...that we are not mediators, because that is the task of Portugal, the United States of America, Russia and the United Nations," he added.
The United Nations and the three countries are overseeing the fitful peace process in Angola, where UNITA waged nearly two decades of civil war after independence from Portugal.

Mandela said South Africa did not want to take over initiatives launched by others. "All that we can do, when we are asked to do so, we will cooperate and render whatever assistance we can... We will not agree to act as mediators," he said.
Savimbi and dos Santos are trying to put a new Angolan government together under a 1994 peace plan that ended the fighting, but progress has been slow.
UNITA has proposed that Savimbi head the official opposition in parliament, rather than be a vice president under dos Santos.
A government of national reconciliation is expected to be installed this month if the problems are solved.
